data."],"material_omissions":["The candidate index includes the National Data Strategy and the interactive federal budget tool, both relevant to information publication and evaluation infrastructure, relevant to the broader correction/evaluation environment."]}],"verdict":"pass_with_corrections","strengths":["The answers consistently distinguish government or institutional evidence from personal Scholz attribution.","They separate enacted policy, appropriations, modeled effects, implementation, and outcomes rather than treating announcements as completed results.","They use the cited passages accurately and preserve important contrary evidence, especially constitutional-budget failure, audit findings, distributional weaknesses, and implementation delays.","They are unusually explicit about uncertainty, period fit, coalition responsibility, and the limits of causal attribution."],"systemic_problems":["Some candidate-index evidence relevant to transparency, lobbying, data infrastructure, and broader economic performance is omitted.","A small number of claims rely on evidence extending beyond 2023 without always foregrounding that limitation.","One malformed phrase reduces editorial reliability in 5B.7."],"concrete_corrections_required":["Correct the malformed phrase \"un具体\" in 5B.7.","Clarify that the DSA evidence in 5B.4 partly concerns 2024 implementation.","Add or acknowledge the omitted 5B.7 evidence on the National Data Strategy and federal budget visualization/data tools.","Consider adding lobbying and party-finance transparency evidence to 5B.5 and the omitted regulatory/investment evidence to 5B.4."],"safe_for_judge_use":true,"rationale":"The answers are substantively reliable and well calibrated against the supplied excerpts. Their central judgments are supported, balanced, and useful for a skeptical judge. Corrections are limited to one malformed phrase, slightly sharper period qualification, and several completeness improvements; none changes the overall direction of the assessments."}
